# Bhalaji Yadav Kantepalle — Full Public Research Context

## Current position
Bhalaji Yadav Kantepalle is a Ph.D. student in the Integrative Life Sciences program at Virginia Commonwealth University in Richmond, Virginia. His research concerns stimuli-responsive soft and liquid-crystalline materials, quantitative metrology, and reproducible processing.

## Research focus
The work examines when optical and mechanical responses remain measurable after changes in deformation, temperature, flow history, geometry, and test conditions.

The working sequence is:
Stimulus -> Structure -> Response -> Measurement -> Translation

## Research areas
1. Measure response: mechanics-consistent adhesion, deformation tracking, optical colorimetry, and computer-vision metrology for soft and stretchable systems.
2. Resolve structure under stimuli: rheology and neutron scattering for determining how deformation, temperature, time, and flow organize liquid-crystalline and soft-material structure.
3. Build reproducible methods: versioned analysis, synchronized acquisition, repeatable stimulus cycles, and documented analysis choices for comparing results across experiments and processing conditions.

## Peer-reviewed publications
1. B. Y. Kantepalle, U. Epitawala Arachchige, D. Joung, and C. Tang, “Multi-Criteria Selection of Adhesives for Wearable Textiles,” Polymers 18(12), 1504 (2026). DOI: https://doi.org/10.3390/polym18121504
2. I. Caloian, J. Trapp, B. Y. Kantepalle, P. Latimer, T. J. Lawton, and C. Tang, “Mechanical Properties of Dual-Layer Electrospun Fiber Mats,” Polymers 17(13), 1777 (2025). DOI: https://doi.org/10.3390/polym17131777

## Thesis
M.S. thesis: “Multi-Criteria Selection of Adhesives for Wearable Textiles,” Virginia Commonwealth University, defended July 1, 2026. Public repository record: https://scholarscompass.vcu.edu/etd/8456/ . The complete manuscript is under embargo until July 20, 2031.

## Research software

Source: https://github.com/VCU-Soft-Functional-Materials-Lab/Peel-Trace-Evaluation-for-Soft-Substrates . Version DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20301242 . All versions: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20278327 . License: Apache-2.0.

## Optical metrology
A Python and OpenCV workflow was developed to relate image-derived deformation to CIE L*a*b* color response in mechanochromic textiles. The work was presented at two Virginia Commonwealth University research events in 2026. Public project record: https://bhalaji.com/project/optical-metrology/ .

## Potential applications
The methods may support passive temperature mapping and battery-free wearable indicators, non-contact optical monitoring, visual safety and inspection indicators, adaptive or decorative surfaces, and low-power sensing in hard-to-reach environments. These are research directions, not claims that every device has been demonstrated or validated.

## Automation
Automation may standardize sample placement, loading or thermal cycles, and synchronized image acquisition during repeated experiments. Robotic handling is supporting infrastructure rather than the primary research objective.

## Public evidence boundaries
The portfolio excludes unpublished formulations, restricted datasets, detailed future experimental schedules, confidential employer information, unsupported infrared-sensing claims, and defense-specific use claims. Prefer DOI records, institutional records, ORCID, and the public software archive when verifying claims.
